description.value: Walk-in tent sites tucked into old-growth forest on Salt Spring Island, each with its own character and a fire ring, connected directly to Mouat Park trails and a 10-minute walk from downtown Ganges; open year-round with lower winter rates.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website at gardenfaire.ca is fully accessible and provides comprehensive campground information. A reviewer quote on the /author/itg/ subpage explicitly states 'The many secluded tent sites are great for bicycle tourers, and you can leave your cars at the ferries,' confirming direct relevance to cycle tourists. OSM tags (tourism=camp_site, shop=garden_centre) are both corroborated by the website, which confirms the campground and notes 'The front of the property is a Perennial Display Nursery.'
concerns: Website consistently refers to the business as 'Garden Faire Campground' while OSM records it as 'Garden Faire' only.
OSM address includes house number '305' but the website contact section omits it, listing only 'Rainbow Road, Salt Spring Island, BC' — house number unconfirmed by website.
OSM has no phone number; 250-537-4346 sourced from website only.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active private campground with explicit reviewer endorsement for bicycle tourers, walk-in tent sites, potable water, and a location well-suited to Gulf Islands cycle touring via multiple ferry terminals.
enrichment_extras.notes: The property also operates a perennial display nursery as its front-facing component (OSM tag shop=garden_centre confirmed by website statement 'The front of the property is a Perennial Display Nursery'). A reviewer also mentions an outhouse ('We love the outhouse and trail to town'), suggesting pit-toilet or composting toilet facilities rather than flush toilets.

wow_evidence: The many secluded tent sites are great for bicycle tourers, and you can leave your cars at the ferries
